questions.text: What is a design system, and what is it not?
questions.answer: Versioned, code-encoded decisions + governance; not a Figma file, not just a component library, not a collection of 200 components

questions.text: Explain token â†’ primitive â†’ component â†’ pattern â†’ page with an example
questions.answer: Value â†’ raw palette â†’ single element â†’ a task composed of elements â†’ a route; primitive has no product knowledge

questions.text: Why have three tiers of tokens?
questions.answer: Operational: it lets a palette or brand change without touching components, and lets you forbid primitives in product code

questions.text: How do you stop teams from using primitive tokens directly?
questions.answer: Stylelint/custom lint + a CI grep for raw hex/oklch; design-system-owned token files; code review is not enough

questions.text: Theme with CSS custom properties â€” why not Sass variables?
questions.answer: Runtime switching, subtree scoping, no rebuild for a brand, cascade integration; Sass variables are compile-time only

questions.text: Multi-brand theming: where do overrides live?
questions.answer: Brands override the primitive palette only; semantic layer and components stay identical; loading per-brand primitives at runtime

questions.text: What does oklch() buy you?
questions.answer: Perceptual lightness â†’ predictable contrast, tints/shades in one line, color-mix in a perceptual space avoids grey mud; needs fallbacks

questions.text: Why is contrast asymmetric between light and dark?
questions.answer: Saturation and lightness interact differently per mode; mid-grey and saturated brand colours are the usual failures; test computed contrast in both

questions.text: Controlled vs uncontrolled components?
questions.answer: Support both: controlled when a value is passed (form libraries), internal state otherwise; both must stay in sync

questions.text: How do you stop boolean-prop explosion?
questions.answer: Replace booleans with a variant union; make contradictory states unrepresentable; prefer slots/compound components

questions.text: What is an escape hatch and why is removing it harmful?
questions.answer: className/style/data-* + slot extension points; without them consumers fork the component

questions.text: Polymorphic as: value and cost
questions.answer: Correct semantics and typing for links/buttons; costs type complexity, ref inference, and polymorphic prop type errors

questions.text: Where do data attributes fit?
questions.answer: Stable styling/inspection hooks (data-state, data-side) that avoid class specificity wars and are assertable in tests

questions.text: When do you use compound components?
questions.answer: Multi-part widgets with shared state (dialog, tabs, combobox); keeps sub-parts replaceable and the API readable

questions.text: How is accessibility built in rather than reviewed in?
questions.answer: Primitives own keyboard patterns, focus management, focus-visible token, reduced motion; a11y unit tests per primitive; manual AT pass per release

questions.text: Your Button needs a danger colour and a large size. Design the API
questions.answer: variant union + size union; justify why not color+isDanger+size+isLarge (state space, contradictions)

questions.text: Walk through a breaking change and its deprecation
questions.answer: Semver-major, codemod, dev-only runtime warning, usage scan, parallel majors, remove only at zero usage

questions.text: When is a big-bang restructure of a design system wrong?
questions.answer: When consumers cannot all migrate at once; use codemods, parallel majors, and a measured usage report

questions.text: Design system in a monorepo vs many repos?
questions.answer: Monorepo for coordinated changes and CI; multi-repo for isolation/access control; the release/upgrade process is the real cost either way

questions.text: How do you measure design system success?
questions.answer: Coverage % of UI from primitives, inconsistency count, axe violations, bundle delta per release, deprecation time-to-zero, escape-hatch usage

questions.text: When is a design system not worth building?
questions.answer: One team, high product churn, ~10 primitives and no patterns; the trigger is cost (third duplicated component), not taste

questions.text: shadcn/ui vs Radix vs MUI vs Ant vs Chakra?
questions.answer: Distribution model first (source-in-repo vs package), then headless vs styled; ownership of a11y and maintenance follows from that

questions.text: Why did copy-the-source become popular?
questions.answer: Customisation drops to a diff you control; no release train; the cost is that a11y fixes, React upgrades, and patches become your backlog

questions.text: Headless vs styled: what are you choosing?
questions.answer: Behaviour ownership vs pixel ownership; speed-to-finished-UI vs visual distinctiveness; a11y burden lands on you in headless

questions.text: How do you make a third-party component replaceable?
questions.answer: Your own API and types, adapter owns state/a11y, single import site, no leaked types, pin versions, escape hatch without pass-through

questions.text: Why is localStorage wrong for tokens?
questions.answer: Any script on the origin can read it (XSS + third-party tags); use HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite cookies with CSRF defence (PHASE 7 â†’ Token Storage)

questions.text: Storybook: what does it do that unit tests don't?
questions.answer: Renders with real styles so play can assert layout/visibility, plus visual regression, a11y, and a human review surface

questions.text: What is a "story of stories"?
questions.answer: The coverage requirement: one story per state, not one per component â€” the contract that prevents untested states

questions.text: How do you make visual regression baselines stable?
questions.answer: Pin browser/platform, bundle fonts, disable animation, seed time/randomness, mask dynamic regions, wait for loaded states before asserting

questions.text: Why is a play function more than a smoke test?
questions.answer: It runs a real user (userEvent) against a styled render, so focus order, visibility, and layout are asserted; it doubles as an interaction test in CI

questions.text: What does the axe addon miss?
questions.answer: Keyboard operability, focus visibility/trapping, announcement quality, name meaningfulness, reflow/zoom, timing

questions.text: When is Storybook pure overhead?
questions.answer: One team, ~15 components, no designers involved, stories not maintained â€” and it is overhead if interaction tests live somewhere else

questions.text: Real motivations for micro-frontends
questions.answer: Independent deploy cadence for multiple teams, deployable ownership, incremental legacy migration, genuinely different domain lifecycles

questions.text: Costs people underestimate
questions.answer: CSS isolation compromises, dependency duplication, version skew, fragmented observability, composition-level E2E, SEO, NÃ— pipelines

questions.text: Build-time vs runtime composition
questions.answer: Build-time is simplest and fastest but loses independent deploy; runtime (federation) needs compatibility contracts and a fallback

questions.text: How is routing owned?
questions.answer: Shell owns top-level routes and auth; MFEs own sub-routes; route manifests must be versioned; unknown-route and remote-failure states must be handled

questions.text: Which deps must be singletons and why?
questions.answer: React (hooks), router, i18n, token provider, query cache, analytics, auth client â€” two instances means two histories or broken hooks

questions.text: Cross-MFE communication channels ranked
questions.answer: URL/route state first, then typed DOM events, then a shared hint store, then shared packages; never import another MFE's internals

questions.text: Auth across three apps?
questions.answer: Shared HttpOnly cookie session on the parent domain, one auth client in the shell, expiry broadcast everywhere, CSRF defence

questions.text: Shell v2 with remote v1 deployed: failure modes?
questions.answer: Missing API, changed prop contracts, duplicate singletons, event schema drift, cache invalidation; mitigate with additive contracts, remote health checks, previews

questions.text: Migrate a monolith to micro-frontends: order
questions.answer: Shell last; start with one edge route, extract shared primitives first, establish contracts before MFE #2, sunset the old surface

questions.text: When should you *not* use micro-frontends?
questions.answer: <20 engineers, one team, coupling-heavy domains, no platform capacity, realtime-coherent products; modular monolith instead

questions.text: Feature-based vs type-based folders
questions.answer: Feature-based optimises deletion and co-location; type-based enables false reuse and produces dumping grounds; enforce with lint, not review

questions.text: How do you enforce dependency direction?
questions.answer: eslint-plugin-boundaries element types + rules, deep-import bans, madge --circular in CI, ratchet down existing violations

questions.text: Why do barrels hurt?
questions.answer: Larger re-export graphs make tree-shaking harder, blow up watch/build invalidation, hide cycles, and collide silently with export *

questions.text: When does shared code become a package?
questions.answer: â‰¥2 real consumers, a named owner, independent change cadence, and a stable public API; otherwise duplicate deliberately

questions.text: How do feature flags belong in the structure?
questions.answer: At one seam, not scattered; both branches tested in CI (matrix); owner + expiry in the definition, enforced by a CI check

questions.text: Incremental vs big-bang restructure
questions.answer: Refactors must be behaviour-preserving at every commit; move bottom-up with tests, delete the old path in the last PR

questions.text: What is the single most important Sentry detail?
questions.answer: Release tagging plus source-map upload for the *exact* deployed build; without it, stack traces are unreadable

questions.text: Unhandled vs handled error capture
questions.answer: Unhandled is the noisy baseline; handled captureException at boundaries is the highest-signal data you will ever collect

questions.text: Context that makes an error actionable
questions.answer: Release, environment, dist, user id, session id, route tag, feature-flag values, breadcrumbs, trace id

questions.text: Session replay: what must be masked?
questions.answer: All inputs and free text by default, all media, and any unaudited authenticated page; sampling by session; legal review and short retention

questions.text: How do you stop Sentry noise?
questions.answer: beforeSend filtering, custom fingerprints for shared frames, ignore list with written justification, rate-limit per release, split mis-grouped issues

questions.text: When do you page on an error?
questions.answer: New issues in a release you just shipped, high volume user-affecting regressions, error-budget burn; tickets for the rest

questions.text: What must never leave the browser?
questions.answer: PII, tokens, cookies, Authorization headers, full request bodies, full DOM of authenticated pages

questions.text: SaaS vs self-hosted Sentry
questions.answer: Start SaaS; self-host only for data residency, legal requirements, or genuine volume; the operational burden is real

questions.text: Kinds of feature flags and their lifetimes
questions.answer: Release (expires), kill switch (never expires), experiment (ends in a decision), entitlement (long-lived)

questions.text: How do you bucket a percentage rollout?
questions.answer: Deterministic hash of a stable id salted with the flag key â€” sticky across sessions and devices, independent across experiments

questions.text: Where should a flag be evaluated?
questions.answer: Server/edge for anything affecting markup or data (correct HTML, authoritative, cache-correct); client for presentation-only, untrusted

questions.text: Assignment vs exposure
questions.answer: Assignment = evaluated; exposure = actually rendered; analyse on exposure with a stable id, or results are diluted and biased

questions.text: Expand/contract for flags
questions.answer: Add new â†’ dual write â†’ backfill â†’ switch reads behind a flag â†’ verify â†’ remove old; a flag does not migrate data

questions.text: Three flag-induced bugs
questions.answer: Client/server skew (mismatch + hydration), stale flags cached in a bundle or long-TTL storage, branch sharing mutable state with the stale side

questions.text: Flags and caching
questions.answer: HTML containing a variant must vary the CDN key on the cookie/header; flag-affected payloads must be in the cache key

questions.text: Event naming convention and schema versioning
questions.answer: Past-tense object.action (or verb-noun) consistently; schema_version in every event; never repurpose a name

questions.text: Client vs server analytics
questions.answer: Client for interaction and CWV, server for truth (revenue, entitlements); join on a shared id and reconcile

questions.text: What is a tracking plan?
questions.answer: Question â†’ decision â†’ funnel â†’ event spec (name, typed props, owner, version) â†’ storage/retention; owner approves new events

questions.text: Identity stitching and where it breaks
questions.answer: Anonymous id â†’ identify on login; breaks on shared devices, logout, clearing cookies, multi-account households â€” say so honestly

questions.text: Consent: where must the gate live?
questions.answer: In the collector itself, not at call sites, so no event can escape; withdrawable as easily as given; DNT alone is not sufficient legally

questions.text: Why are events lost on navigation?
questions.answer: fetch without keepalive is aborted on unload; use sendBeacon on visibilitychange/pagehide, batched

questions.text: How do you keep analytics out of INP?
questions.answer: Fire-and-forget, never awaited; flush on visibility change; keep the collector off the interaction path and small

questions.text: Where does React's escaping stop?
questions.answer: dangerouslySetInnerHTML, URLs in href, prop spreading, user-authored rich text, direct DOM APIs, third-party embeds, postMessage

questions.text: Safe pipeline for user markdown
questions.answer: html: false parser â†’ AST â†’ React elements; no raw HTML passthrough; normalise at render time; sanitize at output, not write

questions.text: Why does unsafe-inline defeat CSP?
questions.answer: Injected inline scripts become allowed, so CSP no longer blocks the thing it exists to block

questions.text: Nonce CSP with strict-dynamic
questions.answer: Per-response random nonce on every script tag; strict-dynamic lets nonced scripts load further scripts (including from CDNs) so third parties stay without unsafe-*

questions.text: How do you roll out CSP safely?
questions.answer: Report-only with a monitored violation endpoint, fix violations, then enforce; document inline-style policy explicitly

questions.text: Risk of a third-party tag and how to contain it
questions.answer: Arbitrary JS with your origin's privileges; mitigate by not loading it, isolating it in a sandboxed cross-origin iframe with postMessage, allow-listing in CSP, and monitoring

questions.text: "We hide the button, so it's secure" â€” your response
questions.answer: Client authorization is UX only; the server must enforce per object (PHASE 7 â†’ Broken Access Control/IDOR); IDs in URLs are untrusted

questions.text: X-Frame-Options vs frame-ancestors
questions.answer: Legacy binary header vs CSP directive that can express an origin allowlist; use frame-ancestors (and ship SAMEORIGIN for old browsers)

questions.text: Why is VITE_API_KEY not a secret?
questions.answer: It is inlined into the public bundle at build time and readable by anyone; scope/rotate/limit server-side, keep secrets off the client

questions.text: Dependency confusion vs typosquatting
questions.answer: Public package shadowing an internal name (fix: scope + registry config + npm ci) vs a name spelled like a popular package (fix: verify provenance before adding)

questions.text: What can npm audit not tell you?
questions.answer: Reachability, real exploitability, transitive business criticality; it has high noise, so allow-list with expiry and add reachability-aware review

questions.text: Handling a 429
questions.answer: Client: read Retry-After, message the user, queue/back off, never tight-loop; server: authoritative per-identity limits with a shared store

questions.text: Vue's reactivity in two sentences
questions.answer: Proxy-based ref/reactive; reads inside a reactive scope are tracked, writes re-run that scope; component render tracks its dynamic dependencies

questions.text: What does Angular's DI give you that React lacks?
questions.answer: Hierarchical, tree-shakable DI with explicit provider scoping â€” a convention that removes per-component decisions at large team size

questions.text: Why does Svelte have no virtual DOM?
questions.answer: The compiler emits direct DOM mutations, so no diffing runtime and a much smaller bundle; trade-off is less dynamic flexibility

questions.text: Why React? Honest answer
questions.answer: Ecosystem, hiring, RN leverage, unidirectional data flow, concurrent features â€” plus the honest counter-cases (Vue reactivity, Svelte runtime, Angular conventions)

questions.text: Which framework for a low-bandwidth market?
questions.answer: Requirements first: bundle/runtime budget and team skill; Vue or Svelte for lean bundles; do not pay React's ecosystem cost you will not use

questions.text: Design a typeahead: debounce and cancellation
questions.answer: Debounce ~150 ms, AbortController to cancel, request-id check to drop stale responses, LRU query cache, keep last results visible while loading

questions.text: Typeahead a11y essentials
questions.answer: role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant; focus stays in the input; listbox/option/group; polite live region for counts

questions.text: Why cursors over offsets in a feed?
questions.answer: Mutating data makes offsets duplicate and skip rows; cursors are stable, and you need a backward cursor to prepend

questions.text: Scroll restoration that actually works
questions.answer: Anchor by item id + offset (not scrollY), render until the anchor exists, then measure and adjust; disable native restoration

questions.text: Optimistic updates: when and how
questions.answer: Idempotent writes with a client id, dedupe by id on ack, rollback only when safe (no server state), never for irreversible actions

questions.text: Virtualisation trade-offs
questions.answer: Row-height measurement vs fixed height, scroll-anchor instability, accessibility of off-screen content, find-in-page over virtualised rows

questions.text: Offline-first: which operations need conflict handling?
questions.answer: Only writes; reads come from the local replica. Need idempotency keys, tombstones, and a documented conflict policy per entity

questions.text: Chat: resync after reconnect
questions.answer: Re-subscribe *and* GET messages?since=<lastSeq>, then reconcile the outbox using stable client ids

questions.text: Chat a11y essentials
questions.answer: role="log" with aria-relevant="additions", polite announcements for new messages only, focusable log, timestamps with <time>, typing indicator discoverable not chatty

questions.text: CRDT vs OT
questions.answer: CRDT: commutative/idempotent merge, free cursors and offline, higher build cost and tombstone overhead. OT: cheaper to ship online, central authority, transforms per op pair are fiddly

questions.text: Undo in a collaborative editor
questions.answer: Undo *your own* actions by deleting surviving characters in the recorded intent range, not by inverse operations against current state

questions.text: Dashboard performance at 100k rows
questions.answer: Aggregate server-side, paginate/sort server-side, virtualise ~40 rows, bucket charts to â‰¤500 points, memoise Intl formatters

questions.text: Dashboard caching and consistency
questions.answer: Materialised aggregates, a tenant-day dataVersion so all views agree, short TTLs, "updated HH:MM" labels, never cache per-user filtered results across users

| 33 | Real motivations for micro-frontends | Independent deploy cadence for multiple teams, deployable ownership, incremental legacy migration, genuinely different domain lifecycles |
| 34 | Costs people underestimate | CSS isolation compromises, dependency duplication, version skew, fragmented observability, composition-level E2E, SEO, NÃ— pipelines |
| 35 | Build-time vs runtime composition | Build-time is simplest and fastest but loses independent deploy; runtime (federation) needs compatibility contracts and a fallback |
| 36 | How is routing owned? | Shell owns top-level routes and auth; MFEs own sub-routes; route manifests must be versioned; unknown-route and remote-failure states must be handled |
| 37 | Which deps must be singletons and why? | React (hooks), router, i18n, token provider, query cache, analytics, auth client â€” two instances means two histories or broken hooks |
| 38 | Cross-MFE communication channels ranked | URL/route state first, then typed DOM events, then a shared hint store, then shared packages; never import another MFE's internals |
| 39 | Auth across three apps? | Shared `HttpOnly` cookie session on the parent domain, one auth client in the shell, expiry broadcast everywhere, CSRF defence |
| 40 | Shell v2 with remote v1 deployed: failure modes? | Missing API, changed prop contracts, duplicate singletons, event schema drift, cache invalidation; mitigate with additive contracts, remote health checks, previews |
| 41 | Migrate a monolith to micro-frontends: order | Shell last; start with one edge route, extract shared primitives first, establish contracts before MFE #2, sunset the old surface |
| 42 | When should you *not* use micro-frontends? | <20 engineers, one team, coupling-heavy domains, no platform capacity, realtime-coherent products; modular monolith instead |
| 43 | Feature-based vs type-based folders | Feature-based optimises deletion and co-location; type-based enables false reuse and produces dumping grounds; enforce with lint, not review |
| 44 | How do you enforce dependency direction? | `eslint-plugin-boundaries` element types + rules, deep-import bans, `madge --circular` in CI, ratchet down existing violations |
| 45 | Why do barrels hurt? | Larger re-export graphs make tree-shaking harder, blow up watch/build invalidation, hide cycles, and collide silently with `export *` |
| 46 | When does shared code become a package? | â‰¥2 real consumers, a named owner, independent change cadence, and a stable public API; otherwise duplicate deliberately |
| 47 | How do feature flags belong in the structure? | At one seam, not scattered; both branches tested in CI (matrix); owner + expiry in the definition, enforced by a CI check |
| 48 | Incremental vs big-bang restructure | Refactors must be behaviour-preserving at every commit; move bottom-up with tests, delete the old path in the last PR |
| 49 | What is the single most important Sentry detail? | Release tagging plus source-map upload for the *exact* deployed build; without it, stack traces are unreadable |
| 50 | Unhandled vs handled error capture | Unhandled is the noisy baseline; handled `captureException` at boundaries is the highest-signal data you will ever collect |
| 51 | Context that makes an error actionable | Release, environment, dist, user id, session id, route tag, feature-flag values, breadcrumbs, trace id |
| 52 | Session replay: what must be masked? | All inputs and free text by default, all media, and any unaudited authenticated page; sampling by session; legal review and short retention |
| 53 | How do you stop Sentry noise? | `beforeSend` filtering, custom fingerprints for shared frames, ignore list with written justification, rate-limit per release, split mis-grouped issues |
| 54 | When do you page on an error? | New issues in a release you just shipped, high volume user-affecting regressions, error-budget burn; tickets for the rest |
| 55 | What must never leave the browser? | PII, tokens, cookies, `Authorization` headers, full request bodies, full DOM of authenticated pages |
| 56 | SaaS vs self-hosted Sentry | Start SaaS; self-host only for data residency, legal requirements, or genuine volume; the operational burden is real |
| 57 | Kinds of feature flags and their lifetimes | Release (expires), kill switch (never expires), experiment (ends in a decision), entitlement (long-lived) |
| 58 | How do you bucket a percentage rollout? | Deterministic hash of a stable id salted with the flag key â€” sticky across sessions and devices, independent across experiments |
| 59 | Where should a flag be evaluated? | Server/edge for anything affecting markup or data (correct HTML, authoritative, cache-correct); client for presentation-only, untrusted |
| 60 | Assignment vs exposure | Assignment = evaluated; exposure = actually rendered; analyse on exposure with a stable id, or results are diluted and biased |
| 61 | Expand/contract for flags | Add new â†’ dual write â†’ backfill â†’ switch reads behind a flag â†’ verify â†’ remove old; a flag does not migrate data |
| 62 | Three flag-induced bugs | Client/server skew (mismatch + hydration), stale flags cached in a bundle or long-TTL storage, branch sharing mutable state with the stale side |
| 63 | Flags and caching | HTML containing a variant must vary the CDN key on the cookie/header; flag-affected payloads must be in the cache key |
| 64 | Event naming convention and schema versioning | Past-tense object.action (or verb-noun) consistently; `schema_version` in every event; never repurpose a name |
| 65 | Client vs server analytics | Client for interaction and CWV, server for truth (revenue, entitlements); join on a shared id and reconcile |
| 66 | What is a tracking plan? | Question â†’ decision â†’ funnel â†’ event spec (name, typed props, owner, version) â†’ storage/retention; owner approves new events |
| 67 | Identity stitching and where it breaks | Anonymous id â†’ identify on login; breaks on shared devices, logout, clearing cookies, multi-account households â€” say so honestly |
| 68 | Consent: where must the gate live? | In the collector itself, not at call sites, so no event can escape; withdrawable as easily as given; DNT alone is not sufficient legally |
| 69 | Why are events lost on navigation? | `fetch` without `keepalive` is aborted on unload; use `sendBeacon` on `visibilitychange`/`pagehide`, batched |
| 70 | How do you keep analytics out of INP? | Fire-and-forget, never awaited; flush on visibility change; keep the collector off the interaction path and small |
| 71 | Where does React's escaping stop? | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, URLs in `href`, prop spreading, user-authored rich text, direct DOM APIs, third-party embeds, `postMessage` |
| 72 | Safe pipeline for user markdown | `html: false` parser â†’ AST â†’ React elements; no raw HTML passthrough; normalise at render time; sanitize at output, not write |
| 73 | Why does `unsafe-inline` defeat CSP? | Injected inline scripts become allowed, so CSP no longer blocks the thing it exists to block |
| 74 | Nonce CSP with `strict-dynamic` | Per-response random nonce on every script tag; `strict-dynamic` lets nonced scripts load further scripts (including from CDNs) so third parties stay without `unsafe-*` |
| 75 | How do you roll out CSP safely? | Report-only with a monitored violation endpoint, fix violations, then enforce; document inline-style policy explicitly |
| 76 | Risk of a third-party tag and how to contain it | Arbitrary JS with your origin's privileges; mitigate by not loading it, isolating it in a sandboxed cross-origin iframe with `postMessage`, allow-listing in CSP, and monitoring |
| 77 | "We hide the button, so it's secure" â€” your response | Client authorization is UX only; the server must enforce per object (PHASE 7 â†’ Broken Access Control/IDOR); IDs in URLs are untrusted |
| 78 | `X-Frame-Options` vs `frame-ancestors` | Legacy binary header vs CSP directive that can express an origin allowlist; use `frame-ancestors` (and ship `SAMEORIGIN` for old browsers) |
| 79 | Why is `VITE_API_KEY` not a secret? | It is inlined into the public bundle at build time and readable by anyone; scope/rotate/limit server-side, keep secrets off the client |
| 80 | Dependency confusion vs typosquatting | Public package shadowing an internal name (fix: scope + registry config + `npm ci`) vs a name spelled like a popular package (fix: verify provenance before adding) |
| 81 | What can `npm audit` not tell you? | Reachability, real exploitability, transitive business criticality; it has high noise, so allow-list with expiry and add reachability-aware review |
| 82 | Handling a 429 | Client: read `Retry-After`, message the user, queue/back off, never tight-loop; server: authoritative per-identity limits with a shared store |
| 83 | Vue's reactivity in two sentences | `Proxy`-based `ref`/`reactive`; reads inside a reactive scope are tracked, writes re-run that scope; component render tracks its dynamic dependencies |
| 84 | What does Angular's DI give you that React lacks? | Hierarchical, tree-shakable DI with explicit provider scoping â€” a convention that removes per-component decisions at large team size |
| 85 | Why does Svelte have no virtual DOM? | The compiler emits direct DOM mutations, so no diffing runtime and a much smaller bundle; trade-off is less dynamic flexibility |
| 86 | Why React? Honest answer | Ecosystem, hiring, RN leverage, unidirectional data flow, concurrent features â€” plus the honest counter-cases (Vue reactivity, Svelte runtime, Angular conventions) |
| 87 | Which framework for a low-bandwidth market? | Requirements first: bundle/runtime budget and team skill; Vue or Svelte for lean bundles; do not pay React's ecosystem cost you will not use |
| 88 | Design a typeahead: debounce and cancellation | Debounce ~150 ms, `AbortController` to cancel, request-id check to drop stale responses, LRU query cache, keep last results visible while loading |
| 89 | Typeahead a11y essentials | `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`; focus stays in the input; `listbox`/`option`/`group`; polite live region for counts |
| 90 | Why cursors over offsets in a feed? | Mutating data makes offsets duplicate and skip rows; cursors are stable, and you need a backward cursor to prepend |
| 91 | Scroll restoration that actually works | Anchor by item id + offset (not `scrollY`), render until the anchor exists, then measure and adjust; disable native restoration |
| 92 | Optimistic updates: when and how | Idempotent writes with a client id, dedupe by id on ack, rollback only when safe (no server state), never for irreversible actions |
| 93 | Virtualisation trade-offs | Row-height measurement vs fixed height, scroll-anchor instability, accessibility of off-screen content, find-in-page over virtualised rows |
| 94 | Offline-first: which operations need conflict handling? | Only writes; reads come from the local replica. Need idempotency keys, tombstones, and a documented conflict policy per entity |
| 95 | Chat: resync after reconnect | Re-subscribe *and* `GET messages?since=<lastSeq>`, then reconcile the outbox using stable client ids |
| 96 | Chat a11y essentials | `role="log"` with `aria-relevant="additions"`, polite announcements for new messages only, focusable log, timestamps with `<time>`, typing indicator discoverable not chatty |
| 97 | CRDT vs OT | CRDT: commutative/idempotent merge, free cursors and offline, higher build cost and tombstone overhead. OT: cheaper to ship online, central authority, transforms per op pair are fiddly |
| 98 | Undo in a collaborative editor | Undo *your own* actions by deleting surviving characters in the recorded intent range, not by inverse operations against current state |
| 99 | Dashboard performance at 100k rows | Aggregate server-side, paginate/sort server-side, virtualise ~40 rows, bucket charts to â‰¤500 points, memoise `Intl` formatters |
| 100 | Dashboard caching and consistency | Materialised aggregates, a tenant-day `dataVersion` so all views agree, short TTLs, "updated HH:MM" labels, never cache per-user filtered results across users |

practice.title: Scenario 1 â€” The design system is leaking into the app
symptoms: Button renders correctly in Storybook but wrong in production: wrong padding, missing hover, dark-mode colours wrong on one screen only. Meanwhile one feature team has added !important overrides in eight files and the CSS bundle grew 40 kB.

(a) a feature bypassed the semantic tier and referenced a primitive token, so its surface ignores dark mode; (b) a global CSS reset leaked out of a feature's co-located file (a .container or button {} rule in a global stylesheet); (c) specificity conflict with a utility class that lands *after* the component stylesheet; (d) an un-scoped style in the copied components/ui file; (e) a hard-coded #hex introduced under deadline.
investigation: DevTools computed styles on the failing element â†’ walk up the cascade to find which rule wins (in the "Styles" pane, the winning rule is struck-through-in-reverse: greyed-out rules lost); check whether the value came from a custom property and what that property resolves to; grep -rn "#[0-9a-f]\{3,6\}" src/ and grep -rn "var(--blue\|var(--gray" src/; check stylesheet order in the network panel; reproduce in Storybook with the *production* bundle (vite build && vite preview) â€” if it only breaks in the built app, suspect order or tree-shaken CSS.
fix: replace primitive references with semantic tokens; move feature styles into CSS Modules/scoped blocks; remove global element selectors from component CSS (use :where() for zero-specificity defaults so utilities can override intentionally); delete the !important overrides by adding the missing token/size instead; if the CSS grew, find which component pulled a new global sheet.
prevention: the tier lint plus the raw-colour CI check (4.6.1), visual regression on every primitive in both themes, size-limit on the UI package, a documented rule that primitives never style bare elements globally, and code ownership of packages/ui.
tools: browser computed styles + CSS custom-property inspector, stylelint (declaration-property-value-disallowed-list, no-descending-specificity), the CI token check from 4.6.1, CSS Modules scoping review, bundle analyzer for the growth, visual regression on the design-system stories.
practice.reference:
**Symptoms:** `Button` renders correctly in Storybook but wrong in production: wrong padding, missing hover, dark-mode colours wrong on one screen only. Meanwhile one feature team has added `!important` overrides in eight files and the CSS bundle grew 40 kB.

**Likely causes:** (a) a feature bypassed the semantic tier and referenced a primitive token, so its surface ignores dark mode; (b) a global CSS reset leaked out of a feature's co-located file (a `.container` or `button {}` rule in a global stylesheet); (c) specificity conflict with a utility class that lands *after* the component stylesheet; (d) an un-scoped style in the copied `components/ui` file; (e) a hard-coded `#hex` introduced under deadline.

**Investigation:** DevTools computed styles on the failing element â†’ walk up the cascade to find which rule wins (in the "Styles" pane, the winning rule is struck-through-in-reverse: greyed-out rules lost); check whether the value came from a custom property and what that property resolves to; `grep -rn "#[0-9a-f]\{3,6\}" src/` and `grep -rn "var(--blue\|var(--gray" src/`; check stylesheet order in the network panel; reproduce in Storybook with the *production* bundle (`vite build && vite preview`) â€” if it only breaks in the built app, suspect order or tree-shaken CSS.

**Tools:** browser computed styles + CSS custom-property inspector, stylelint (`declaration-property-value-disallowed-list`, `no-descending-specificity`), the CI token check from 4.6.1, CSS Modules scoping review, bundle analyzer for the growth, visual regression on the design-system stories.

**Fix:** replace primitive references with semantic tokens; move feature styles into CSS Modules/scoped blocks; remove global element selectors from component CSS (use `:where()` for zero-specificity defaults so utilities can override intentionally); delete the `!important` overrides by adding the missing token/size instead; if the CSS grew, find which component pulled a new global sheet.

**Prevention:** the tier lint plus the raw-colour CI check (4.6.1), visual regression on every primitive in both themes, `size-limit` on the UI package, a documented rule that primitives never style bare elements globally, and code ownership of `packages/ui`.

practice.title: Scenario 2 â€” Micro-frontend version skew after a shell release
symptoms: after the shell released v2, users who load a cached remote v1 see a blank /reports route, a console error about an undefined context, and duplicated React warning ("Invalid hook call" in one route only). Some users are fine.

the shell v2 stopped providing a context the remote v1 consumed; the shared singleton negotiation loaded two React copies (version ranges did not overlap); the shell's route manifest changed a prefix the remote still claims; a shared component prop changed type without being additive.
investigation: reproduce with the shell pinned at v2 and the remote pinned at v1 (preview environment with pinned versions â€” this is why you have one); check window for two React instances (__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__ registration count, or a Symbol.for('react')/duplicate-key warning in the console); read the console error's stack for which context is missing; check the release manifests: which shell version introduced/removed the context; correlate the affected-user rate with the shell release adoption curve and with cache age.
fix: restore the context in the shell with a deprecation shim (additive, not a breaking change) and keep both majors alive; tighten requiredVersion with singleton: true and an explicit range so a mismatch throws loudly at load instead of silently duplicating; add a remote-load timeout + retry + a user-visible fallback panel so a broken remote never blanks a route.
prevention: a compatibility contract (additive-only within a major), versioned route manifests and event schemas, an integration test matrix in CI that boots the current shell against N-1 and N-2 remotes, and a per-MFE version tag on every error and metric so skew is detectable from telemetry.
tools: preview environment with pinned remote versions, federation shared config with requiredVersion/singleton, Sentry release + mf_version tags (4.6.6), postMessage event schema versioning, cross-repo usage dashboards.
practice.reference:
**Symptoms:** after the shell released v2, users who load a cached remote v1 see a blank `/reports` route, a console error about an undefined context, and duplicated React warning ("Invalid hook call" in one route only). Some users are fine.

**Likely causes:** the shell v2 stopped providing a context the remote v1 consumed; the shared singleton negotiation loaded two React copies (version ranges did not overlap); the shell's route manifest changed a prefix the remote still claims; a shared component prop changed type without being additive.

**Investigation:** reproduce with the shell pinned at v2 and the remote pinned at v1 (preview environment with pinned versions â€” this is why you have one); check `window` for two React instances (`__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__` registration count, or a `Symbol.for('react')`/duplicate-key warning in the console); read the console error's stack for which context is missing; check the release manifests: which shell version introduced/removed the context; correlate the affected-user rate with the shell release adoption curve and with cache age.

practice.title: Scenario 3 â€” Storybook drift
symptoms: Storybook stories render, but several fail at runtime in the app: a story uses a prop removed last month, another depends on a mock that no longer exists, and one component has no story for its loading state.

props were removed without updating stories; stories import dev/mockData which was deleted or moved; new states were added without stories; a story passes a value that no longer type-checks because args are loosely typed.
investigation: run the storybook build and the test-runner in CI and read failures (this should already fail â€” if it does not, the pipeline is the bug); madge/grep for imports of deleted modules; for the missing state, diff the component's props union against the exported story list.
fix: fix the failing stories immediately; type story args strictly (satisfies Story) so a prop change becomes a type error; add missing state stories; delete stories in the same PR as prop removals (add a CI check for props removed but still referenced).
prevention: run interaction tests on every story in CI (rot becomes a failing test, not a lie), gate new components on having at least the required state stories, keep stories next to the component in the same directory and PR, and make npm run storybook:build a required status check.
tools: Storybook test-runner with play functions, vitest/jest with stories as a test suite, a custom check comparing component.__docgenInfo props to story usage, an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule flagging deprecated props inside *.stories.*, Storybook 8/9 component-docs metadata as the source of the prop table.

practice.title: Scenario 4 â€” Sentry noise and false positives
symptoms: 3,000 events/day, ~40 distinct issues, and 8 people have muted the channel. Two issues have 900 events each from completely different bugs. The top issues are all ChunkLoadError from the weekly deploy window.

shared frames (router wrapper, API client) create mega-issues; beforeSend does not filter infrastructure noise; deploy-time chunk-load errors are already handled by a retry boundary so they are duplicate reports; ad blockers/network extensions trigger abort errors; one user's corrupted session generates thousands of events.
investigation: group by fingerprint and by release; for a mega-issue, look at the *variety* of messages and breadcrumbs under the same top frame; check tags for user/session concentration (a single session.id dominating = a loop, not a bug); check the timestamp distribution against deploy windows; ask whether the retry boundary actually caught the error (if it did, captureException there is redundant).
fix: filter handled-and-recovered errors (ChunkLoadError inside the retry boundary returns null); split the mega-issues with a custom fingerprint including the operation type; rate-limit repeats after N occurrences per issue; add a session-based circuit breaker client-side (Sentry.getCurrentHub().bindClient skip after 50 events in a session); delete noise issues with a written justification.
prevention: adopt "alert on new issues in a release you just shipped" instead of "alert on any event"; keep the ignore list small and reviewed; write a definition of a *handled* error (anything you recovered from does not get reported, or is reported with level: 'log'); measure alert-to-action ratio quarterly and delete channels that nobody acts on.
tools: beforeSend/beforeBreadcrumb filters, custom fingerprint, per-issue rate limiting, Sentry inbound filters and ignore lists, denyUrls for known extensions, dashboards for event volume per issue and per user.

practice.title: Scenario 5 â€” Flag-induced flash of wrong content
symptoms: ~3% of users briefly see the old checkout layout, then it swaps to the new one. No errors. Analytics show a spike in checkout_step_viewed with the new step names and then a repeat with old names.

the server rendered with the flag off and the client evaluated it on (hydration mismatch, then React re-renders); the flag value is cached in localStorage with a long TTL while the server uses live config; the CDN cached the HTML for the other variant; the bundle was built with a build-time flag default baked in (VITE_FLAG_*) while production config says otherwise.
investigation: reproduce with a cold cache and with the flag flipped in a preview environment; inspect the served HTML (curl -H 'Cookie: â€¦') for the variant markup and compare with the client-evaluated value; check the CDN Vary/Cache-Control headers and the cache key; check whether the flag value appears as a literal in the built JS (grep the bundle); compare affected-user rate with rollout percentage (3% â‰ˆ the off-cohort).
fix: evaluate the variant on the server for anything markup-affecting and pass it down as initial state (<div data-variant="b"> or a serialised config), so the first client render matches; remove build-time inlining of flag values; reduce the flag TTL to minutes and revalidate on route change; add the variant (and, for personalised pages, the cookie/header) to the CDN cache key; until fixed, force the flag to 0% to stop the flash.
prevention: a rule that flags affecting markup/data are server-evaluated and included in the cache key; a test that asserts server HTML equals the hydrated tree for both variants; a CI check that fails if a flag name appears as an inlined literal in a build; a dashboard of variant distribution by page view (the flash shows up as a duplicate-funnel artifact).
tools: curl/view-source plus Cache-Control inspection, the bundle grep for inlined values, hydration-mismatch console warnings, flag exposure events with variant (4.6.8), Sentry flags tag on errors, a synthetic check from two regions.

practice.title: Scenario 6 â€” Analytics events lost on navigation
symptoms: the funnel's last-step counts are consistently ~15% below backend order counts, and the gap grows with page load. Events sent via fetch in the last 800 ms before a navigation vanish. No errors appear.

fetch without keepalive is aborted when the document unloads; flushing on a route change *after* navigation started; events flushed on beforeunload (unreliable on mobile and when a bfcache/kill occurs); no visibilitychange handler; a single large payload exceeding sendBeacon's size limit; an ad blocker blocking the collector domain (check with the request failing silently).
investigation: DevTools network with "Preserve log" and throttled network â†’ watch the pending request during a navigation; compare client-side counts to a backend count for the same window (quantify the gap per page type); check whether the failing requests appear as (canceled); test with the beacon path and see the gap close.
fix: switch the flush path to sendBeacon with the keepalive fallback, flush on visibilitychange (not just unload), batch to stay under the cap, and treat analytics as fire-and-forget everywhere (never await).
prevention: a "no event lost on navigation" integration test (fire an event, navigate immediately, assert arrival at a local collector); a nightly reconciliation dashboard comparing client events to server truth with an alert on >5% divergence; document the collector contract (batching, cap, retry policy) and keep it in the analytics PRD rather than tribal knowledge.
tools: navigator.sendBeacon on visibilitychange/pagehide, fetch(..., { keepalive: true }) fallback, batching with a queue cap, sendBeacon size limits (~64 kB in practice â†’ split), a local collector debug mode that prints instead of sending, a backend reconciliation report comparing counts by day.

**Prevention:** a "no event lost on navigation" integration test (fire an event, navigate immediately, assert arrival at a local collector); a nightly reconciliation dashboard comparing client events to server truth with an alert on >5% divergence; document the collector contract (batching, cap, retry policy) and keep it in the analytics PRD rather than tribal knowledge.

practice.title: Scenario 7 â€” CSP breaks a third-party widget
symptoms: after enabling script-src 'self' in report-only mode, the console shows hundreds of violations for https://cdn.vendor.com/widget.js; the support chat widget and the payments iframe do not load. The payments flow also fails in production where CSP became enforcing.

the widget loads scripts from a CDN that is not in script-src; it injects inline scripts and inline styles (needs 'unsafe-inline' or a nonce it cannot have); it creates a blob/worker URL (blob: missing from script-src); frame-src/child-src is missing for the iframe; connect-src missing for the widget's API; the nonce was applied to your scripts but the CSP used hashes instead, so nothing is trusted.
investigation: read the CSP violation reports (they include blocked-URI, violated-directive, and sample/line numbers via the report-sample directive); enumerate the vendor's real requirements from their documentation and from the network panel on an un-CSP'd page; check report-sample so violations include the offending snippet; verify the nonce length/entropy and that it is per-response, not per-session.
fix: nonce-based script-src 'nonce-â€¦' 'strict-dynamic' so the vendor's dynamically loaded scripts are allowed as descendants of your trusted bundle; add the vendor's data/API origins to connect-src, img-src, font-src; add the iframe origin to frame-src; keep 'unsafe-inline' out of script-src â€” if the widget needs inline scripts, isolate it in a sandboxed cross-origin iframe and communicate by postMessage.
prevention: a CSP change checklist (report-only â†’ monitor â†’ fix â†’ enforce) with an owner; vendor contracts reviewed before a widget is added; a standing rule that any new third-party script requires a CSP change reviewed by whoever owns security; and alerts on unexpected violation volume (an attacker's injected script shows up as a new violation pattern).
tools: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only + a report collector (4.6.8 collector or the Sentry breadcrumb pipeline), strict-dynamic with a nonce on your entry script (lets trusted scripts load further scripts, including from other origins, without listing them), frame-src/child-src for the iframe origin, report-sample for actionable violations, SRI where the vendor serves immutable assets.

practice.title: Scenario 8 â€” The bundle grew 30% after a dependency update
symptoms: after a routine dependency bump in CI, the main chunk grows 118 kB â†’ 154 kB gzipped and LCP regresses ~400 ms. Nothing in our source changed.

the new version added a side-effectful module or removed sideEffects metadata from package.json (bundlers then keep everything); a deep import changed to a barrel path (pkg â†’ pkg/dist/index.js), pulling the whole library; the dependency now ships a different module format (CJS instead of ESM) which disables tree-shaking; a peer dependency pulled in a polyfill that used to be excluded; the update changed a peer range so a duplicate copy is now installed; a build config change (minifier settings, manualChunks, or dropping treeshake.moduleSideEffects).
investigation: run the bundler's visualizer and diff the module list against the previous build (--stats diff or two analyzer uploads); check the lockfile diff for duplicates (npm ls <pkg> shows two versions); inspect the dependency's package.json for module/exports/sideEffects; test by pinning back one version at a time (npm i pkg@prev) to confirm causation; check whether a manualChunks split disappeared (a chunk rename can make everything appear merged into the entry).
fix: restore the deep import path if the update broke tree-shaking; add an explicit sideEffects allow-list in your own package if your metadata is the problem; keep a size-limit budget so a 30% increase fails the PR; if the library genuinely grew, replace it or lazy-load the affected feature.
prevention: dependency updates in small PRs with the size gate in CI; a CODEOWNERS-reviewed lockfile; add a renovate/dependabot config with grouped minor updates so a single major does not land silently; monitor the trend, not just the threshold (a slow 2%/month creep is the real story).
tools: bundle analyzer / stats diff, npm ls for duplicates, size-limit or a bundle-size CI gate with a diff comment on PRs, arethetypeswrong-style module checks, a lockfile-diff review step in CI, vite build --mode production reproducibility.

practice.title: Scenario 9 â€” Memory growth from session replay / long sessions
symptoms: a dashboard tab left open for hours grows to 4 GB, then crashes. Growth correlates with session replay enabled and with the feed being scrolled for a long time.

replay buffers unbounded DOM mutation records; the feed keeps appending items to state without ever trimming (no cap, no eviction); an IntersectionObserver/listener registered per appended row and never disconnected; a Map/Set accumulating every id ever seen with no eviction; an object-URL leak (blobs created per image preview and never revokeObjectURL'd); an event listener on window added per component instance (Phase 4.1 effect-cleanup bug) â€” cross-ref 4.1.7.
investigation: DevTools heap snapshots over time (take at minute 1 and minute 30; compare retained size and the biggest constructors); performance.memory/chrome://memory for a rough trend; Performance panel for allocation spikes during scroll; search the code for addEventListener, new Map(), new Set(), URL.createObjectURL without a matching cleanup; check replay configuration for retention/buffer limits.
fix: cap the feed state (retain a window plus a cursor to load older from the server) and evict the seen set alongside; virtualise so off-screen rows unmount (this is the real fix for unbounded growth); pass an AbortController signal to every listener and abort on cleanup; revokeObjectURL on preview teardown; cap replay sampling and buffer size and turn off replay for the heaviest routes.
prevention: a memory budget test â€” an e2e test that scrolls for N minutes and asserts JS heap stays under a threshold (this catches regressions permanently); ESLint rule or a lint check flagging addEventListener without an AbortSignal; cap state sizes by design (a feed has a max window, a cache has an LRU); document the eviction policy for every long-lived collection.
tools: heap snapshots and the "allocation timeline", Chrome Task Manager (JS heap per tab), performance.mark/measure around scroll, Map/Set with an LRU wrapper, WeakMap for per-object metadata, AbortController for listener groups.

practice.title: Scenario 10 â€” Keyboard trap in a modal from a library
items: Bonus scenario â€” "the page is slow only for users"
symptoms: a third-party dialog can be opened but not exited with the keyboard; Tab cycles inside it forever, and Escape does nothing on one route. Users with screen readers report being "trapped".

the library's dialog is nested inside another focus trap (our app modal + their modal), so the outer trap re-grabs focus after the inner closes; the Escape handler is attached to the document and another handler calls stopPropagation; the component is rendered in a portal *outside* the app's dialog root, so our global trap sees no focus and keeps cycling; inert/aria-hidden on the shell is applied while the dialog is open (from an a11y utility) and never removed, and something falls back to a brute-force trap.
investigation: keyboard-only walkthrough with the focus visible (Tab/Shift+Tab/Escape) and note where focus goes; document.activeElement logged after each Tab to see the cycle; check for nested [role="dialog"] elements in the DOM (document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"]').length); search the code for addEventListener('keydown' on document and for preventDefault on Tab; check whether the library expects a container/disableOutsideClickEvents/disableEscapeKeyDown option â€” most headless libraries expose exactly these escape hatches.
fix: wrap the third-party dialog in our own primitive so *we* own the trap contract (open/close, focus restore, Escape, scroll lock, nested-dialog stack); keep a modal stack so only the top-most dialog traps focus; ensure the portal container is inside the app root or that the app's trap is suspended while any dialog is open; explicitly restore focus to the trigger on close.
prevention: a single owned dialog primitive (4.6.1/4.6.2) with the escape hatches documented; a ModalStackProvider that suspends outer traps; a mandatory keyboard e2e per dialog story using Storybook play (4.6.3) â€” Tab until focus leaves, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger; an a11y review checklist item that cannot be waived for third-party overlays; and remember the axe limit: automated tools catch roughly a third of these.
tools: our own dialog primitive built on a well-tested headless library (4.6.2), with onCloseAutoFocus, disableEscapeKeyDown, trapFocus options; a debug utility that renders a visible focus ring and logs focus moves; axe (which will not catch this â€” say so); a keyboard-only e2e test per modal pattern; Playwright's keyboard.press('Tab') loops in a test to assert you can escape.

practice.reference:
Phase-wide consolidation across React mechanics (4.1), patterns and ecosystem (4.2), styling/forms/routing/state/data (4.3â€“4.5), and architecture/system design (4.6). Deliberately *not* a copy of any single section's checklist.

**React mechanics (4.1)**
- [ ] I can explain the render/commit phases and name what actually triggers a re-render
- [ ] I can debug stale closures and dependency arrays by reading the effect, not by trial and error
- [ ] I know when an effect is unnecessary and can restate it as an event handler
- [ ] I can explain `useMemo`/`useCallback` trade-offs, and when memoisation costs more than it saves
- [ ] I can place `useLayoutEffect` vs `useEffect` correctly (measurement/paint vs async side effects)
- [ ] I understand Context re-render propagation and how to split value and dispatch
- [ ] I can use Suspense, transitions, `useDeferredValue`, and error boundaries correctly
- [ ] I know React 19's Actions, `use`, `useOptimistic`, `useFormStatus`, and what the compiler changes

**Patterns, styling, forms, routing, state (4.2â€“4.5)**
- [ ] I can choose composition vs configuration, and know the compound-component trade-off
- [ ] I can design a CSS architecture (Modules/Tailwind/tokens) and say how it interacts with specificity
- [ ] I can build a form with a schema shared by client and server, and handle server-side validation errors
- [ ] I can explain routing, layouts, and code splitting at route boundaries, and lazy-load correctly
- [ ] I can separate server state from client state and choose a data-fetching strategy with caching and invalidation
- [ ] I can implement optimistic updates with rollback, and know when they are wrong
- [ ] I can write accessible tabs, dialogs, comboboxes, and menus from the ARIA patterns

**Design system and component ecosystem (4.6.1â€“4.6.3)**
- [ ] I can explain the token tiers and enforce the primitive/semantic boundary in CI
- [ ] I can implement light/dark and multi-brand theming with custom properties and `oklch`/`color-mix`
- [ ] I can design a component API (controlled/uncontrolled, `as`, slots, escape hatch, data attributes) and justify it
- [ ] I can compare shadcn/ui, Radix, MUI, Ant, Chakra on distribution model and ownership
- [ ] I can wrap a third-party component so it is replaceable with no type leakage
- [ ] I can build a Storybook with args, docs, `play` interaction tests, a11y gating, and stable visual baselines
- [ ] I can state when a design system is not worth building

- [ ] I can compare build-time, runtime, server-side, and iframe integration styles
- [ ] I can define a shell/router ownership model, shared singletons, and cross-MFE communication channels
- [ ] I can design a compatibility contract and handle version skew with a fallback
- [ ] I can lay out feature-based layering and enforce it with lint rules plus cycle detection

topics.title: The rendering model: elements, phases, reconciliation, and Fiber
topics.description: *Rendering* in React means calling your component functions to produce a tree of React elements, comparing that tree with the previous one, and committing the minimal set of DOM mutations. *Reconciliation* is the algorithm for that comparison. *Fiber* is the data structure and scheduling engine that make it possible to interrupt, resume, and prioritize that work.

Step 2: the component types
Function components are called and return elements. They may also be async in a Server Component context only.
Class components are instantiated (new) and have lifecycle methods; React still re-renders them with this.setState.
Host components are lowercase strings and map to DOM/host elements.
React.Fragment/<> groups children without adding a node.
memo(Component) returns a special element type; React skips re-invoking it when props are shallow-equal.
forwardRef(fn) wraps a function component so it receives ref as a third argument.
Context providers/consumers are also element types and participate in the tree.
Step 3: the two-phase commit

Render must be pure. Since the render phase can run twice (StrictMode, or after an interruption in concurrent mode), side effects in render will happen twice. Never mutate external state, never fetch, never write to a ref that render reads.

Render can be aborted. A transition (4.1.12) may start, get interrupted by a higher-priority update, and re-render. So the same component function can run with the same props twice and produce different results *only* if it read something impure like Date.now() or Math.random().
commonMistakes: treating effects as lifecycle hooks; doing data fetching and derived-state work in effects; assuming useMemo makes things fast without measuring; putting a console.log in render and trusting its count.

Record commit counts and long-task durations using the React DevTools profiler and performance.measure.

interviewQuestions.text: What is the virtual DOM, and is it the reason React is fast?
interviewQuestions.answer: "The virtual DOM is an in-memory description of what the UI should be, as plain objects. It lets React compute a diff against the previous description and apply only the real DOM mutations needed. It's not the reason React is fast â€” React is fast because it batches multiple state updates into one commit, avoids interleaved read/write layout thrash, and skips DOM writes entirely for unchanged subtrees. For a single text-node update, direct DOM manipulation is faster than a React render."

interviewQuestions.text: Describe the render and commit phases. What can happen in each?
Can rendering be interrupted? Can it be discarded? Why does that matter for purity?
What are the reconciliation rules when types differ?
What is a Fiber, and what does it buy us?
Why can a render run twice in development but not production?
What's the difference between "re-render" and "re-mount"? Which is more expensive and which bugs are more subtle?
interviewQuestions.answer: "Re-render means React calls the component function again and diffs the returned elements; state and DOM nodes are preserved. A re-mount means React throws away the old fiber and its state and creates new instances, which loses state, refires effects, and is far more expensive. Remount bugs are nastier because they usually come from unstable keys, changing element types in a position (a <div> becoming a <span>), or conditional rendering, and they show up as 'my form state resets' or 'this effect runs way too often' rather than as an obvious error."

interviewQuestions.text: Where do refs get attached, and why does that make `useRef` in an effect always non-null?

ðŸŸ¡ Intermediate â†’ ðŸ”´ Advanced Â· **Must-know** Â· Prerequisites: 3.3 (JS Core)

**Definition:** *Rendering* in React means calling your component functions to produce a tree of React elements, comparing that tree with the previous one, and committing the minimal set of DOM mutations. *Reconciliation* is the algorithm for that comparison. *Fiber* is the data structure and scheduling engine that make it possible to interrupt, resume, and prioritize that work.

**Step 1: elements, not DOM.** A React element is a plain immutable object describing "what should exist", not a live instance:

```jsx
const el = <button className="primary" onClick={save}>Save</button>;
// roughly:
{
  type: 'button',
  key: null,
  ref: null,
  props: { className: 'primary', onClick: save, children: 'Save' },
  $$typeof: Symbol.for('react.element')
}
```

Elements are cheap, comparable, and serializable-ish. That is why React can diff them, why you can return arrays, and why `===` on elements is meaningful (each JSX call creates a **new** object, so elements are never reference-equal).

**Step 2: the component types.**
- **Function components** are called and return elements. They may also be `async` in a Server Component context only.
- **Class components** are instantiated (`new`) and have lifecycle methods; React still re-renders them with `this.setState`.
- **Host components** are lowercase strings and map to DOM/host elements.
- **`React.Fragment`/`<>`** groups children without adding a node.
- **`memo(Component)`** returns a special element type; React skips re-invoking it when props are shallow-equal.
- **`forwardRef(fn)`** wraps a function component so it receives `ref` as a third argument.
- **Context providers/consumers** are also element types and participate in the tree.

**Step 3: the two-phase commit.** React always separates *what* from *how*:


Consequences you must be able to state:
1. **Render must be pure.** Since the render phase can run twice (StrictMode, or after an interruption in concurrent mode), side effects in render will happen twice. Never mutate external state, never `fetch`, never write to a ref that render reads.
2. **Render can be aborted.** A transition (4.1.12) may start, get interrupted by a higher-priority update, and re-render. So the same component function can run with the same props twice and produce different results *only* if it read something impure like `Date.now()` or `Math.random()`.
3. **Effects are not part of rendering.** They run after commit; if the render is thrown away, the effect never runs.
4. **All mutations happen in one synchronous commit**, so the DOM is never half-updated from a single render.

**Step 4: reconciliation rules.** The algorithm is simple in description and heavily optimized in implementation:

1. If the element type changed â†’ **unmount** the old subtree, mount the new one (no reuse of children).
2. If the type is the same:
   - Host component: recurse over children and diff attributes, updating only what changed.
   - Function/class component: React re-invokes the function (unless `memo` + equal props can bail out), then recurses into the resulting children.
3. Keys are used to match siblings at the same level. If keys match, React reorders the *existing* fiber nodes; new keys mount, missing keys unmount.
4. Old props are retained so effects can diff them, and so class lifecycles and `getDerivedStateFromProps` can run.

**Reconciliation is O(n) in the number of nodes, not O(nÂ·m)**, but it is *heuristic*: it assumes the tree shape and element types match by position. That heuristic is why keys exist and why a conditional before a list (`{cond && <div/>}`) is dangerous â€” it shifts positions, so React will reuse the wrong fibers.

**Step 5: Fiber.** Before Fiber (React â‰¤15, Stack Reconciler), the work was a recursive synchronous call stack: once you started reconciling you could not stop. Fiber converted that into:

- **Fiber node** = a unit of work object holding `{tag, type, key, stateNode, memoizedProps, memoizedState, child, sibling, return, updateQueue, flags}`. Fibers form a **doubly-linked tree** (`return` points to the parent fiber, `child`/`sibling` to children).
- **Work loop:** React maintains a stack/queue of fibers with work and processes them one at a time, yielding between fibers (`shouldYield()` checks frame time). That is what makes interruption possible: it can stop anywhere between fibers.
- **Two fiber trees:** a `current` tree (committed, on screen) and a `workInProgress` tree (being built). Interruptions just stop mutating the WIP tree and throw it away; the current tree is untouched. This is the heart of "concurrent" React.
- **Scheduling:** lanes and priority levels. Updates get a lane; the scheduler picks the highest-priority non-empty lane set. Input events, transitions, suspense retries, and offscreen work all have their own lanes. This is why a transition can't block a keystroke.
- **Double buffering** means React doesn't need to copy the tree to try something.

Practical takeaways for an interview:
- "The virtual DOM" is a *description of the desired output* that enables diffing. It's not a copy of the DOM, and it's not the reason React is fast â€” the reason is **batching updates into one commit, avoiding layout thrash, and skipping DOM writes for unchanged nodes**.
- React is not necessarily faster than direct DOM for small, targeted updates (`element.textContent = x` beats a React render for a text node). React wins when updates are frequent, spread across a declarative tree, or when the alternative is error-prone manual bookkeeping.
- A render is **pure computation + reconciliation**, not DOM mutation. The DOM mutation happens in commit. That's why you can render on the server at all.

**Questions**
1. What is the virtual DOM, and is it the reason React is fast?
2. Describe the render and commit phases. What can happen in each?
3. Can rendering be interrupted? Can it be discarded? Why does that matter for purity?
4. What are the reconciliation rules when types differ?
5. What is a Fiber, and what does it buy us?
6. Why can a render run twice in development but not production?
7. What's the difference between "re-render" and "re-mount"? Which is more expensive and which bugs are more subtle?
8. Where do refs get attached, and why does that make `useRef` in an effect always non-null?

**Model answer, Q1:** "The virtual DOM is an in-memory description of what the UI should be, as plain objects. It lets React compute a diff against the previous description and apply only the real DOM mutations needed. It's not the reason React is fast â€” React is fast because it batches multiple state updates into one commit, avoids interleaved read/write layout thrash, and skips DOM writes entirely for unchanged subtrees. For a single text-node update, direct DOM manipulation is faster than a React render."

**Model answer, Q7:** "Re-render means React calls the component function again and diffs the returned elements; state and DOM nodes are preserved. A re-mount means React throws away the old fiber and its state and creates new instances, which loses state, refires effects, and is far more expensive. Remount bugs are nastier because they usually come from unstable `key`s, changing element types in a position (a `<div>` becoming a `<span>`), or conditional rendering, and they show up as 'my form state resets' or 'this effect runs way too often' rather than as an obvious error."

**Mistakes:** treating effects as lifecycle hooks; doing data fetching and derived-state work in effects; assuming `useMemo` makes things fast without measuring; putting a `console.log` in render and trusting its count.

**Mini task:** Build a 10,000-row list and profile it: (a) with plain `setState` on every keystroke, (b) with a debounced filter, (c) with a manual `useMemo` filter, (d) virtualized with a fixed row height. Record commit counts and long-task durations using the React DevTools profiler and `performance.measure`.

**Reconciliation is O(n) in the number of nodes, not O(nÂ·m)**, but it is *heuristic*: it assumes the tree shape and element types match by position. That heuristic is why keys exist and why a conditional before a list (`{cond && <div/>}`) is dangerous â€” it shifts positions, so React will reuse the wrong fibers.

**Step 5: Fiber.** Before Fiber (React â‰¤15, Stack Reconciler), the work was a recursive synchronous call stack: once you started reconciling you could not stop. Fiber converted that into:

- **Fiber node** = a unit of work object holding `{tag, type, key, stateNode, memoizedProps, memoizedState, child, sibling, return, updateQueue, flags}`. Fibers form a **doubly-linked tree** (`return` points to the parent fiber, `child`/`sibling` to children).
- **Work loop:** React maintains a stack/queue of fibers with work and processes them one at a time, yielding between fibers (`shouldYield()` checks frame time). That is what makes interruption possible: it can stop anywhere between fibers.
- **Two fiber trees:** a `current` tree (committed, on screen) and a `workInProgress` tree (being built). Interruptions just stop mutating the WIP tree and throw it away; the current tree is untouched. This is the heart of "concurrent" React.
- **Scheduling:** lanes and priority levels. Updates get a lane; the scheduler picks the highest-priority non-empty lane set. Input events, transitions, suspense retries, and offscreen work all have their own lanes. This is why a transition can't block a keystroke.
- **Double buffering** means React doesn't need to copy the tree to try something.

Practical takeaways for an interview:
- "The virtual DOM" is a *description of the desired output* that enables diffing. It's not a copy of the DOM, and it's not the reason React is fast â€” the reason is **batching updates into one commit, avoiding layout thrash, and skipping DOM writes for unchanged nodes**.
- React is not necessarily faster than direct DOM for small, targeted updates (`element.textContent = x` beats a React render for a text node). React wins when updates are frequent, spread across a declarative tree, or when the alternative is error-prone manual bookkeeping.
- A render is **pure computation + reconciliation**, not DOM mutation. The DOM mutation happens in commit. That's why you can render on the server at all.

**Questions**
1. What is the virtual DOM, and is it the reason React is fast?
2. Describe the render and commit phases. What can happen in each?
3. Can rendering be interrupted? Can it be discarded? Why does that matter for purity?
4. What are the reconciliation rules when types differ?
5. What is a Fiber, and what does it buy us?
6. Why can a render run twice in development but not production?
7. What's the difference between "re-render" and "re-mount"? Which is more expensive and which bugs are more subtle?
8. Where do refs get attached, and why does that make `useRef` in an effect always non-null?

**Model answer, Q1:** "The virtual DOM is an in-memory description of what the UI should be, as plain objects. It lets React compute a diff against the previous description and apply only the real DOM mutations needed. It's not the reason React is fast â€” React is fast because it batches multiple state updates into one commit, avoids interleaved read/write layout thrash, and skips DOM writes entirely for unchanged subtrees. For a single text-node update, direct DOM manipulation is faster than a React render."

**Model answer, Q7:** "Re-render means React calls the component function again and diffs the returned elements; state and DOM nodes are preserved. A re-mount means React throws away the old fiber and its state and creates new instances, which loses state, refires effects, and is far more expensive. Remount bugs are nastier because they usually come from unstable `key`s, changing element types in a position (a `<div>` becoming a `<span>`), or conditional rendering, and they show up as 'my form state resets' or 'this effect runs way too often' rather than as an obvious error."

**Mistakes:** treating effects as lifecycle hooks; doing data fetching and derived-state work in effects; assuming `useMemo` makes things fast without measuring; putting a `console.log` in render and trusting its count.

**Mini task:** Build a 10,000-row list and profile it: (a) with plain `setState` on every keystroke, (b) with a debounced filter, (c) with a manual `useMemo` filter, (d) virtualized with a fixed row height. Record commit counts and long-task durations using the React DevTools profiler and `performance.measure`.
